\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منظوری} (manzūrī)}{منظوری (manzūrī)}]{\ur{منظوری} (manzūrī) — approval; sanction}

\label{lesson:UR-C383-manzuri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for deserving, then the Urdu for to tidy up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منظوری}}
\textbf{\ur{منظوری}} — \emph{manzūrī} — \textquotedblleft{}approval; sanction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{منظوری} \ur{مل} \ur{گئی} \ur{تو} \ur{کام} \ur{کل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar manzūrī mil gaī to kām kal ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If approval comes through, the work will be done tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منظوری}} (\emph{manzūrī}) is built on \emph{manzūr}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{manẓūr}, \textquotedblleft{}looked at; accepted\textquotedblright{}, with the noun ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manzūrī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manzūrī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar manzūrī mil gaī to kām kal ho gā.} — If approval comes through, the work will be done tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for deserving, then the Urdu for to tidy up, then say \emph{manzūrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{منظوری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Approval; sanction\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انتظام} (intizām)}{انتظام (intizām)}]{\ur{انتظام} (intizām) — an arrangement}

\label{lesson:UR-C383-intizam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to tidy up, then the Urdu for approval.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انتظام}}
\textbf{\ur{انتظام}} — \emph{intizām} — \textquotedblleft{}an arrangement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{آئیں} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{کھانے} \ur{کا} \ur{انتظام} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp āeṅ ge to khāne kā intizām ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you come, there will be food laid on.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انتظام}} (\emph{intizām}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{intiẓām}, \textquotedblleft{}being put in order\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to tidy up, then the Urdu for approval, then say \emph{intizām} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قطعی} (qatī)}{قطعی (qatī)}]{\ur{قطعی} (qatī) — absolute; (with \ur{نہیں}) not at all}

\label{lesson:UR-C383-qati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for approval, then the Urdu for an arrangement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قطعی}}
\textbf{\ur{قطعی}} — \emph{qatī} — \textquotedblleft{}absolute; (with \ur{نہیں}) not at all\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{قطعی} \ur{بات} \ur{نہیں} \ur{کروں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh āyā to maiṅ qatī bāt nahīṅ karūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he comes, I will not speak to him at all.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قطعی}} (\emph{qatī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qaṭʿī}, \textquotedblleft{}decisive\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{qaṭʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}cutting\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qatī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar voh āyā to maiṅ qatī bāt nahīṅ karūṅ gā.} — If he comes, I will not speak to him at all.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for approval, then the Urdu for an arrangement, then say \emph{qatī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بٹورنا} (baṭornā)}{بٹورنا (baṭornā)}]{\ur{بٹورنا} (baṭornā) — to rake in (money, praise); to gather up}

\label{lesson:UR-C383-batorna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an arrangement, then the Urdu for absolute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بٹورنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بٹورنا}} — \emph{baṭornā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rake in (money, praise); to gather up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{فلم} \ur{چلی} \ur{تو} \ur{خوب} \ur{پیسے} \ur{بٹورے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih film chalī to khūb paise baṭore gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this film does well, it will rake in a lot of money.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{خوب} \ur{پیسے} \ur{بٹورے}, \emph{us ne khūb paise baṭore}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بٹورنا}} (\emph{baṭornā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{baṭornā}, \textquotedblleft{}to collect\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vartula}, \textquotedblleft{}round\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11365): to bring things round into a heap, and so to gather in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṭornā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṭornā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar yih film chalī to khūb paise baṭore gī.} — If this film does well, it will rake in a lot of money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an arrangement, then the Urdu for absolute, then say \emph{baṭornā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بٹورنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To rake in (money, praise); to gather up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا} (fel honā)}{فیل ہونا (fel honā)}]{\ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا} (fel honā) — to fail an exam}

\label{lesson:UR-C383-fel-hona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for absolute, then the Urdu for to rake in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا}}
\textbf{\ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا}} — \emph{fel honā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fail an exam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{نہیں} \ur{پڑھا} \ur{تو} \ur{فیل} \ur{ہو} \ur{جاؤ} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne nahīṅ paṛhā to fel ho jāo ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you do not study, you will fail.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لڑکا} \ur{امتحان} \ur{میں} \ur{فیل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh laṛkā imtihān meṅ fel ho gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا}} (\emph{fel honā}) is built from \emph{fel}, borrowed from English \emph{fail}, and \textbf{\ur{ہونا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fel honā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fel honā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne nahīṅ paṛhā to fel ho jāo ge.} — If you do not study, you will fail.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for absolute, then the Urdu for to rake in, then say \emph{fel honā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{فیل} \ur{ہونا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fail an exam\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
